narration.full_text: Trigonometry is fundamentally about the relationships between the sides and angles of a triangle. To understand these relationships, we primarily focus on right-angled triangles. Let's define the three primary trigonometric ratios: sine, cosine, and tangent. For any acute angle in a right triangle, the sine of the angle is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the length of the hypotenuse. Cosine is the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse. And tangent is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side. These three ratios are foundational, but there are also their reciprocals: cosecant, secant, and cotangent. Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, secant is the reciprocal of cosine, and cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent. Together, these six ratios allow us to solve for unknown sides and angles in right-angled triangles, forming the basis of trigonometry.
